text:
Dubai registered 13,707 residential sales valued at AED 39,487,272,167 in the four weeks to 19 November 2026, a 24.1% increase in volume and 23.1% in value compared to the prior period. Mortgage registrations, which are recorded separately from sales, totaled 5,505. The market remains heavily weighted toward off-plan transactions, which accounted for 56.7% of all registered sales during this window.

The median residential price per square foot rose 3.4% to AED 1,727. Top performing areas by volume include Dubai South with 2,736 sales and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,478 sales over the last 12 weeks. Dubai Creek Harbour recorded the highest median price at AED 2,529.7 per square foot, while Majan and Dubai Land Residence Complex traded near AED 1,415 per square foot.

Rental activity showed 107,551 Ejari contracts with a 51.9% renewal rate. The median annual residential rent stood at AED 68,000. Estimated gross yields were highest in International City Phase 1 at 8.6% and Zaabeel First at 8.5%, both for flats. Town Square followed at 7.0%, while Dubai Sports City and Dubai Production City recorded yields of 6.6% and 6.4% respectively.

Price momentum varied significantly across communities. Al Yufrah 1 saw the sharpest 12-week price increase at 34.9%, followed by Dubai Industrial City at 10.1%. Conversely, Saih Shuaib 1 experienced the steepest decline at 29.5%, with Al Hebiah First down 14.9%. The anomaly monitor flagged 972 sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35% away from their comparable median. Figures reflect registered DLD data and Ejari contracts, using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
